story_type: elderly man swept from his car into a flooded river, Guard rescuer rides the hoist into the current
hook: He was 81, and the flood had swept him out of his car.
narration: He was eighty one, and the flood had swept him out of his car.
It happened at a flooded intersection near Taylorsville, California, in February 2017.
A California National Guard Black Hawk crew was flying over the flooding nearby. They were diverted to him.
From above, he was a speck in the debris.
The water around him was more than six feet deep and churning.
A crew member rode the hoist cable down into the current.
A hoist rescuer stays clipped to the cable the whole time, so the river cannot carry him off too.
He pushed through the branches and wrapped his arms around the man.
[short pause] Then the cable lifted them both straight up out of the river.
outcome: The crew hoisted the 81-year-old out of the flood, and the Guard said their quick work saved his life.
title: 81 and swept into a flooded river
description:
A California National Guard HH-60 Black Hawk crew, diverted from flood reconnaissance, hoists an 81-year-old man from turbulent floodwater in Plumas County, California, on Feb. 10, 2017.
